product.olivetti-m290.summary: A professional desktop with its CPU on a replaceable card, designed to let the computer grow without replacing the entire system.
product.olivetti-m290.history: Olivetti introduced the M290 in its professional PC-compatible range alongside the 386-based M380 models. Computerwoche announced on 29 April 1988 that sales would start in May; the Centre for Computing History dates it to 1984, a discrepancy that remains unresolved. The Olivetti Nederland brochure targeted MS-DOS, OS/2 and XENIX work, networking and terminal emulation. It offered 1 MB for DOS and proposed the 2 MB version as an entry to OS/2. A replaceable CPU card was the upgrade argument for its compact case. This sheet covers the 12 MHz M290 with UC081/UC090 boards; M290-25, M290-30 and M290 SP require separate identification. Sources: Olivetti PC M290 brochure, Computerwoche report, record CH41372 and service guide, chapter 5.
product.olivetti-m290.warning: Historical sheet under research. An inherited implementation exists, but this sheet does not enable profile creation or certify a current boot.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.market: Sources disagree on when it went on sale. Computerwoche (29 April 1988) announces availability in May 1988; the Cambridge museum records 1984. No publication date has been identified in the Dutch brochure.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.configur: Buyers could tailor storage and operating systems to their work. The brochure offers 1 or 2 MB, 20, 40 or 100 MB hard disks, 1.2 or 1.44 MB floppy drives and a 40 MB tape drive; these are not one configuration or necessarily bundled software.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.architec: The main logic sits on a replaceable CPU card. The guide identifies UC081/UC090, a 12 MHz 80286, optional 80287 coprocessor, EVA/ADAMO gate arrays and 82C206; it distinguishes configuration, memory and DMA registers.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.memory: Additional cards could expand memory. The brochure offers an initial 1–2 MB and up to 14 MB with expansions; the guide also documents 512 KB on the CPU card and switch settings for MEM 25-292 cards. The commercial maximum is not the emulator limit.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.video: The monitor depends on the installed graphics card. The brochure lists EGA-compatible OEC, VGA-compatible OVC and PGC; the guide identifies them as GO491, GO481 and GO423. There is no single integrated video system common to every configuration.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.expansio: Some slots already hold the computer’s own cards. The brochure lists three 8-bit and five 16-bit slots, with one and three free respectively; it also documents RS-232C and Centronics.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.firmware: Preserved files identify revisions without proving operation. PDPB 1.17 is 64 KiB: its version string is at 0xE02B and the date 06/23/88 is in the text at 0xE009. The PEP3 1.25 file also contains a version and date, but physical attribution remains pending; it is not automatically interchangeable with 1.17.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.verified: Code review confirms that BluMach retains the m290 model inherited from 86Box. Its initialization loads m290_pep3_1.25.bin at F0000h and uses EVA logic. The preservation record reports earlier tests with PDPB 1.17; this session checked files and code only, without running the machine.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.limitati: The firmware tested earlier still needs to be reconciled with the file requested by the current model. The code fixes the clock at 12.5 MHz and allows up to 2 MB, against the documented 12 MHz and expansions up to 14 MB. Boot, storage and peripherals have not been validated here; the sheet remains under research with profile creation disabled.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.brochure: Olivetti Nederland B.V., Olivetti PC M290, two pages, no date identified: architecture, configurations, dimensions and a commercial photograph. Original preserved; image prepared separately for the website, not included in BluMach.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.manual: Olivetti Personal Computer — Pocket Service Guide, chapter 5, pp. 5-1–5-7: UC081/UC090, memory, video, BIOS and I/O maps. Original copy preserved.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.press: Computerwoche, 29 April 1988: May availability announcement alongside the M380 range. Report snapshot preserved.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.museum: Centre for Computing History, record CH41372: 1984 date, conflicting with the 1988 report. Preserved and cited as a discrepancy, not a reconciled date.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.firmware: PDPB 1.17 dump, Internet Archive. SHA-256: 375b1819f4d86136fbb4d6a144a7084270f474c94269983c5ad902a7f51853ee. Local custody; firmware is not distributed.
product.olivetti-m290.technical.source: BluMach 88f74ba3, machine_at_m290_init and m290 entry; compared with the 86Box fork at 6a43d7973. Implementation inspection, not a real-hardware test.
